text:
"All roads lead to Rome" is an idiom meaning that many different paths eventually arrive at the same destination. It nods to the Roman road network radiating from the Forum, where the gilded Milliarium Aureum marked distances from the city. The team note is inaccurate: not every European road was Roman, and the network served military, administrative, and trade purposes rather than existing solely to reach the capital.

CONFIDENCE: 90
